changes: Merged p2 'śrīsanma(!) varmaṇaḥ' into p3 Rāmavarman. 'sanma(!)' is almost certainly a misreading of 'rāma' (śrīrāmavarmaṇaḥ). The same colophon names the Setu's author as rāmavarmaṇa, so both refer to one commentator, son of Himmativarman. Confidence is now medium.
Moved the son_of relation to the merged person (Rāmavarman son_of Himmativarman).
Himmativarman: the titles field now holds the virudāvalī as an epithet. Role stays relative_only, and confidence is medium because the name could be a form of Himmat(a)varman.
Notes expanded: no scribe is named, and the date may belong to the commentary rather than to the copy.

persons.name: Rāmavarman
persons.evidence: himmati varmaṇa putrasya śrīsanma(!) varmaṇaḥ kṛtāv adhyātma rāmāyaṇa setau; ṭīkeyaṃ rāmavarmaṇakṛtā

notes: The catalogue's 'Scribe: Śrīrāma Varmā' is a mistake. Rāmavarman, son of Himmativarman, is the author of the Setu commentary ('ṭīkeyaṃ rāmavarmaṇakṛtā'), not the copyist. No scribe is named. 'śrīsanma(!)' is read as 'śrīrāma'. The figure '9 6' / '96' after 'navamaḥ sargaḥ' looks like a running sarga count. The date 'saṃvat 1801 (mītī) Kārttika vadi 5, Monday' comes straight after the commentary's closing verse. It may therefore date the commentary (or a copy reproduced with it) rather than this manuscript, so treat it as the copying date only with caution. Taking the era as VS gives 1744 CE (October/November). The weekday has not been verified.
